paper.title: KNN and K-means in Gini Prametric Spaces
paper.source_of_truth: arXiv v3 LaTeX e-print, single file arxiv.tex; rendered v3 PDF used to verify proposition, section, page, and supplementary equation numbering.
paper.scope_note: The paper's named mathematical core consists of two prametric definitions and four propositions. Propositions 1 and 2 are finite algebraic properties of monotone ascending-rank and antitone transformed descending-rank profiles. Proposition 3 imports the Cover–Hart asymptotic nearest-neighbor theorem but does not establish its locality assumptions for the sample-dependent Gini prametric. Proposition 4's supplementary argument contains an invalid centroid-minimization step: differentiating the squared objective omits its residual factor, and the claimed arithmetic-mean minimizer has a fixed-rank counterexample. The formalization proves the prametric properties, the algebraic Cover–Hart bound under an explicit locality hypothesis, the counterexample, and corrected conditional descent results without presenting unsupported claims as proved.

items.label: Definition 1
items.name: Empirical Gini prametric

background_notation.X: an n by d real data matrix
background_notation.R_Xj: the ascending empirical rank in feature column j

hypotheses: x_i and x_k are rows of the same data matrix X.
Ranks use the average-rank convention for ties.
items.statement_informal: The Gini prametric sums, over coordinates, the product of the value difference and the corresponding ascending-rank difference.
items.proof_as_in_paper: This is a definition. The paper motivates it as an empirical version of sum_j (x_j-y_j)(F_j(x_j)-F_j(y_j)), where F_j is the j-th marginal cumulative distribution function.
items.formalization_notes: The Lean definition is over an arbitrary finite coordinate type and takes the coordinatewise ascending-rank profiles as data. Proposition 1 supplies their required monotonicity.

lean.route_note: The finite coordinate type replaces the paper's explicit indices 1 through d without changing the formula.

items.label: Proposition 1
items.name: Properties of the Gini prametric
hypotheses: The coordinatewise empirical ascending-rank profile is monotone in the coordinate value.
For linear invariance, the data and rank profiles are transported by the same common translation.
For rank invariance, the same scalar is added to both rank profiles.
items.statement_informal: The Gini prametric has nullity, rank-nullity, non-negativity, symmetry, common-translation invariance, and common-rank-shift invariance.
items.statement_formal: d_G(x,x)=0; equal rank profiles imply d_G(x,y)=0; d_G(x,y)>=0; d_G(x,y)=d_G(y,x); translating both points and their rank profile leaves d_G unchanged; adding a common scalar to the rank profile leaves d_G unchanged.
items.proof_as_in_paper: The paper states: 'Straightforward from the properties of the Gini-covariance.' No algebraic details are supplied.
items.proof_technique: Coordinatewise order compatibility and cancellation in finite sums.
items.proof_completeness: asserted from external Gini-covariance properties, not derived in the paper
external_dependencies: Yitzhaki and Schechtman (2013), properties of Gini covariance.
known_issues_in_paper: The proof does not state which Gini-covariance property supplies each item. The essential non-negativity condition is monotonicity of empirical ascending ranks; the other items follow algebraically.
items.formalization_notes: Each property is a separately named theorem. The non-negativity proof splits on the order of each coordinate and uses monotonicity of its ascending-rank profile.

added_hypotheses: Coordinatewise monotonicity of ascending ranks, made explicit from the paper's empirical-rank construction.
lean.route_note: Direct finite-sum proofs replace the paper's one-line appeal to Gini covariance.

items.label: Definition 2
items.name: Generalized Gini prametric

background_notation.Rbar_Xj: descending empirical rank in feature column j

hypotheses: x_i and x_k are rows of the same data matrix X.
items.statement_informal: The generalized prametric replaces ascending ranks by the (ν-1)-st powers of descending ranks and changes the overall sign.
items.proof_as_in_paper: This is a definition, motivated by the generalized Gini mean difference GMD_ν(X,Y) = -2ν Cov(X,Rbar_F_Y(Y)^(ν-1)) for ν>1.
items.formalization_notes: The Lean core takes the transformed descending-rank score as an argument, while generalizedGiniPrametricOfRank restates Definition 2 with the paper's descending ranks and real exponent ν-1.

lean.route_note: Packaging the powered descending rank as a score isolates the exact algebra used by Proposition 2.

items.label: Proposition 2
items.name: Properties of the generalized Gini prametric
hypotheses: ν > 1 as required by Definition 2.
Each powered descending-rank score t ↦ Rbar(t)^(ν-1) is antitone.
items.statement_informal: The generalized Gini prametric has both nullity properties, non-negativity, symmetry, and common-translation invariance.
items.statement_formal: d_{G,ν}(x,x)=0; equal transformed rank profiles imply d_{G,ν}(x,y)=0; d_{G,ν}(x,y)>=0; d_{G,ν}(x,y)=d_{G,ν}(y,x); common translation of points and rank profiles leaves d_{G,ν} unchanged.
items.proof_as_in_paper: The paper states: 'Straightforward from the properties of the Gini-covariance.' No algebraic details are supplied.
items.proof_technique: Coordinatewise antitonicity and cancellation in finite sums.
items.proof_completeness: asserted from external Gini-covariance properties, not derived in the paper
external_dependencies: Yitzhaki and Schechtman (2013), properties of generalized Gini covariance.
items.formalization_notes: The proof is the sign-reversed analogue of Proposition 1. Antitonicity of the transformed descending-rank score is exposed rather than hidden in a covariance citation.

added_hypotheses: Descending ranks are nonnegative and antitone, the empirical-rank properties used to prove that their (ν-1)-st powers are antitone.
lean.route_note: Direct finite-sum proofs replace the paper's one-line appeal to generalized Gini covariance. The paper-notation non-negativity theorem derives antitonicity of the powered score from ν>1 and the order properties of descending ranks.

items.label: Proposition 3
items.name: Gini KNN convergence and multiclass asymptotic error bound
hypotheses: The global averaging step is represented on a finite probability space.
The generalized Gini nearest-neighbor rule satisfies the Cover–Hart locality/convergence identity.
ν > 1, the domain in which Definition 2 defines d_{G,ν}.
items.statement_informal: Under the Cover–Hart nearest-neighbor convergence hypotheses, the generalized-Gini one-nearest-neighbor error is at least the Bayes error and at most the stated multiclass quadratic bound.
items.proof_as_in_paper: The paper states that the proof is exactly the same as Cover and Hart (1967), that convergence is true for any type of metric used, and that the error-rate bound does not change.
items.proof_technique: Cover–Hart nearest-neighbor convergence plus a finite posterior-probability inequality and concavity/Jensen step.
items.proof_completeness: relies on external Cover and Hart (1967); applicability to the paper's sample-dependent non-metric prametric is not established
external_dependencies: Cover and Hart (1967), nearest-neighbor convergence and asymptotic error identity for suitably smooth distributions on a metric feature space.
known_issues_in_paper: Definition 2 assumes ν>1, while Proposition 3 says all ν≠1 and therefore also includes values outside the definition's stated domain.

The cited Cover–Hart theorem is a metric-space result. The paper does not prove the locality/convergence hypothesis for its sample-dependent generalized Gini prametric, so the citation alone does not discharge the Gini-specific convergence step.
items.formalization_notes: Prove the multiclass Cover–Hart algebra from finite posterior class probabilities, then state a paper-notation bridge whose only extra assumption is the exact nearest-neighbor locality/convergence identity missing from the paper.

added_hypotheses: The global expectation is formalized as a finite weighted average; extending the averaging step to an arbitrary probability measure is not part of this development.
The generalized Gini neighbor rule satisfies the Cover–Hart locality/convergence identity; this is the paper-specific applicability step not supplied by the cited metric-space theorem.
lean.route_note: CoverHartBound.lean proves the pointwise multiclass probability inequality. KNNConvergence.lean proves the finite weighted averaging/Jensen step and the displayed global bound conditional on the two pointwise Cover–Hart premises. Those premises isolate the unproved prametric-specific convergence step instead of treating it as automatic.

items.label: Proposition 4
items.name: Gini K-means convergence under constant ranks
hypotheses: ν > 1, the domain in which Definition 2 defines d_{G,ν}.
Rank vectors remain constant during each center variation.
Assignments choose a nearest current center.
Center updates are arithmetic means, as in the paper and implementation.
items.statement_informal: The paper claims that Gini K-means converges whenever rank vectors stay constant.
items.statement_formal: The iterative assignment and arithmetic-mean center-update procedure based on d_{G,ν} reaches a fixed clustering.
items.proof_as_in_paper: For points assigned to cluster C_k at iteration t, the paper first states d_{G,ν}(x_i,c_k^t)^2 <= d_{G,ν}(x_i,c_k^{t-1})^2 by the assignment step. It then seeks to prove Eq. (1), the corresponding within-cluster sum inequality. For a fixed cluster C it defines f(z) = sum_{i in C}[-sum_j(z_{ij}-z_j)(Rbar_Z(z_{ij})^(ν-1)-Rbar_Z(z_j)^(ν-1))]^2. Holding ranks constant, it writes f'(z)=0 => 2 sum_i sum_j (z_{ij}-z_j)(Rbar_Z(z_{ij})^(ν-1)-Rbar_Z(z_j)^(ν-1))=0, rewrites this as an inner-product equality, and concludes z = (1/n)sum_i z_i. It therefore declares the arithmetic mean the unique minimizer and Eq. (1) true when the displayed rank-vector difference is nonzero.
items.proof_technique: Claimed Lloyd descent: nearest-center assignment followed by a purported arithmetic-mean minimization of the fixed-cluster objective.
items.proof_completeness: gap: the derivative of the squared objective omits the residual factor, and the resulting arithmetic-mean minimizer claim is false
known_issues_in_paper: Definition 2 assumes ν>1, while Proposition 4 says all ν≠1.
Differentiating the sum of squared Gini distances must retain the outer distance residual; the supplementary derivative omits it.

Even with fixed ranks, the arithmetic mean need not minimize the squared Gini objective. For ν=2 and one-dimensional points 0, 1, and 10, both 11/6 and the arithmetic mean 11/3 lie in the same rank cell, but the squared objectives are 485/6 and 101 respectively.
The repository's Gini inertia adds the raw Gini distance although the supplementary proof uses its square; the Gini branch ignores the squared=True argument.
items.formalization_notes: Formalize the exact fixed-rank counterexample, derive the correct one-dimensional weighted least-squares center for the squared objective, and prove a conditional termination theorem under a natural-valued strict-descent hypothesis. The Lean status records these proved conditional replacements, not an unconditional proof of the paper's claim.

added_hypotheses: For the corrected centroid result, fixed-rank score gaps give nonnegative squared weights, the center satisfies the weighted normal equation, and positive total weight is assumed for uniqueness.
For termination, every non-fixed iteration strictly decreases a natural-valued potential.
lean.route_note: The corrected weighted least-squares minimizer and uniqueness theorems, the fixed-rank counterexample, and termination under a natural-valued strictly decreasing potential are proved. Because the arithmetic-mean minimizer used in the paper is false, the formalization proves this explicitly conditional replacement and does not assert that the original argument succeeded.

items.label: Derived check for Proposition 4
items.name: Fixed-rank counterexample to the arithmetic-mean minimizer step
items.kind_note: Lean-checked diagnostic of the key minimization step in the supplementary proof.

human.statement: Supplementary Materials, 'Proof of Proposition 4', the arithmetic-mean minimizer paragraph after Eq. (1)

hypotheses: The one-dimensional cluster consists of 0, 1, and 10.
The candidate center remains in the fixed-rank cell (1,10), giving descending ranks 4,3,2,1 to 0,1,z,10.
items.statement_informal: A center in the same fixed-rank cell has strictly smaller squared Gini objective than the arithmetic mean.
items.proof_as_in_paper: The paper claims the opposite general minimization property; this derived check evaluates its objective directly in a fixed-rank cell.
items.proof_technique: Exact rank substitution and polynomial normalization.
items.formalization_notes: The Lean proof instantiates the generalized Gini definition itself, proves the three distances 2z, z-1, and 10-z, expands the squared objective, and checks both rational values exactly.

lean.route_note: This is a direct evaluation of the paper's fixed-rank squared objective, not a surrogate model.
